items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: I was playing up at Minton’s with all kinds of wonderful people, Carmen McRae and Tony Scott and playing with all these wonderful people.

ctx.x: So there was a pretty healthy recording and live music scene at that time.

Oh yeah, oh wonderful. You know when people ask me now to go back in your life and pick out a time that you really, the time that you most enjoyed, and I would have to say the time I spent with Billy. Because not only was it a good trio and playing good music and all like that, it was a real brotherly kind of thing that we had, Billy and I had, and also I was playing — when Billy wasn’t working — I was playing up at Minton’s with all kinds of wonderful people, Carmen McRae and Tony Scott and playing with all…

In retrospect, when you think about playing with Coltrane and Miles and Charlie Parker, is there things that stick out in you mind that maybe at the time didn’t make an impression on you but in later years? That’s an awful big question.
